ruling: The owner has directed that nodes talk to the relay directly instead of being routed through the Mac agent.
today: A browser action traverses relay -> D1 job -> Mac agent -> browser spool -> extension poll. Two brains and two queues to move one click. The Mac routes work it has no opinion about, and a sleeping Mac makes the browser unreachable even though browser and relay are both awake.
target: The Safari extension holds its own outbound WebSocket to the relay; the relay pushes commands straight down it and results return the same way.

iPhone control becomes its own node with its own relay connection. It CANNOT leave the Mac — window capture and event posting are both Mac-local — so the hop removed is a function call, not a network trip; the gain is independent identity, liveness and failure domain.
The D1 job row stays as the durable record and reconnect catch-up, exactly as the Mac doorbell socket already does (BridgeHub Durable Object, commit 1967f48, one hub per device).
The Mac agent keeps OBSERVING both surfaces so the Hive dashboard and the action ledger do not go blind. Subscribe, do not route.
prerequisite: Every node needs its own scoped device credential. Today the pendant firmware and the Mac bridge both authenticate with the relay ADMIN key, and the scoped-token system (pdt_ tokens, roles, revocation, /v1/devices/pair) is fully built on the relay and called by nobody.

ownerRulings: No deterministic per-tool guardrails. Every tool enabled by default; the model asks only when about to act BEYOND what the owner requested.
No hardcoded capability lists in the first-level prompt. Tools are discovered hierarchically: domains, then tools, then schemas.
The pendant must work standalone — the phone is not always with the owner, so audio cannot depend on it.
Root-cause audio faults before adding buffering.
